page: Microsoft Azure E4bds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The system is driven by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor based on x86_64 architecture. It provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The CPU configuration features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX-512 and cryptographic acceleration. System memory totals 32.0 GB, providing an allocation ratio of 8.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. The instance also includes 161 GB of bundled local SSD storage, while omitting dedicated GPU hardware accelerators.

Performance testing across standard benchmarks indicates moderate single-thread compute capabilities alongside lower multi-threaded throughput, aligned with its 4-vCPU sizing. Single-core evaluation via stress-ng reaches 1897.78 and Geekbench yields 1455.0, both settling within average performance tiers. In contrast, multi-threaded results, such as a PassMark CPU score of 5878.51 and a multi-core Geekbench score of 3107.0, rank in lower benchmark percentiles. Uncached large-block memory read bandwidth measures 29.48 GB/sec with write throughput at 25.57 GB/sec. Application testing displays 4.03 million Redis SET operations per second and 6.48 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The architectural trade-off of the E4bds_v5 pairs lower aggregate compute throughput with elevated memory density and high-speed local disk capacity. This hardware distribution delivers favorable efficiency for workloads where memory footprint and local disk responsiveness take priority over raw multi-core scaling. Best-fit use cases include in-memory key-value stores, moderate database servers, static content delivery, and enterprise services that require 32 GB of RAM but operate effectively on a 4-vCPU envelope.
description: Microsoft Azure E4bds_v5 is a memory-optimized cloud server built on the Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 4 dedicated vCPUs across 2 physical cores, 32.0 GB of system memory, and 161 GB of local SSD temporary storage without discrete GPU hardware. Single-core compute and data decompression benchmarks display average performance, while multi-core processing throughput reflects the compact 4-vCPU resource profile. With an 8:1 memory-to-core ratio, the server yields strong resource density for tasks that demand elevated memory capacity rather than intensive parallel CPU calculation. The configuration is appropriate for running in-memory caching systems such as Redis, relational databases, static web hosting, and memory-dependent business software.
